notes.summary: Actual PRIMARY geometric pullback and compact quotient regularization; full-support continuous kernels force openness.
notes.detailedSummary: Uses entire qualified G331/G345 at their exact scopes. Proves actual source blowup closed in finite base change, all-support Cartier pullback, literal closed image, compact fibre-maximum USC identity without openness, and open pointwise identity. Normal-domain kernels give openness only when every source minimal component dominates.
notes.text:
Let R be excellent reduced local, a proper primary ideal, and X_R the ENTIRE centered real-semivaluation section v(a)=1. Supports are arbitrary primes below the marked maximal ideal. For finite reduced B use its whole semilocal section X_B with gauge aB, before closed-center decomposition. Dimension-zero reductions have empty sections.

The correctness supports are precisely entire qualified G331 and G345. G331 constructs the independent geometric core on actual PRIMARY blowups using actual negative-effective finite REAL exceptional Cartier presentations with nonnegative degree on every contracted integral curve. Its continuous uniform class C equals the ideal closure; D consists of actual infima of decreasing C-nets, including bottom. It proves positive C,D descent under every reduced finite injection exactly for functions constant on EVERY restriction fibre, and supplies the full normalization conductor quotient and normal-domain full-support norm kernels. G345 supplies independently supported Cartier products on bounded D, arity dim R−1, ordinary OPEN locality, weak uniform continuity, and bounded decreasing-NET continuity with prescribed D limit. Neither grant supplies the new finite-map or envelope conclusions. Their entire manuscripts, mandatory source ledgers, corrections and scopes accompany the new paper unchanged. Smooth specialization means their CLOSED smooth affine algebraically closed characteristic-zero BFJ scope, plus direct DVR/empty cases.

Finite pullback is geometric on the core. For primary I, the degreewise surjection Rees_R(I) tensor_R B → Rees_B(IB) puts Bl_IB(B) as a closed subscheme of the finite base change of Bl_I(R). Thus the actual source model is finite over the base model. This is proved for GLOBAL finite semilocal B; an individual localization B_q need not be finite as an R-module. The source Rees algebra is reduced. Each surviving positive-dimensional component has generic point outside the exceptional fibre: a component mapped entirely to the closed point is zero-dimensional and has no centered boundary. An exceptional Cartier equation is nonzero on every surviving generic component, hence regular on the reduced source. Actual effectivity therefore pulls back. On a contracted integral curve mapping to a curve, pulled line-bundle degree is the image degree times the full function-field degree, with closed residue-field conversion; when the image is a point its degree is zero. These are numerical intersections on proper FIELD curves, not global Chow degrees. Negative effectivity and curve-nefness pull back. Evaluation uses Frac(B/Q) for the actual support Q and its valued lattice with generic trivialization, so restriction recovers base evaluation on EVERY support. Common product-primary refinements preserve this. The granted comparison and the two authorized completions then give pullback on C,D without arbitrary-model cofinality.

Every finite map factors through A=R/ker(R→B), which is reduced. Support-quotient valuation extension from G331 makes X_B→X_A a compact surjective quotient; X_A is literally the closed subset v(ker)=∞ of X_R. For injections write rho:X_B→X_R. Normalization fibres are singletons at finite conductor value; at infinite conductor value they are exactly equal restrictions through S/c→R/c. Vertical and lower-dimensional points remain.

For bounded-above extended F on compact Hausdorff X define F*(x)=inf_{U containing x} sup_U F. If rho:Y→X is a continuous compact-Hausdorff surjection, then (F composed with rho)*(y)≤F*(rho(y)) and F*(x)=max_{rho(y)=x}(F composed with rho)*(y). The first inequality follows by pulling back neighborhoods. The USC function on a compact fibre attains its maximum, including the all-bottom case. For the converse take any finite t above that maximum. Each fibre point has an open neighborhood where F composed with rho<t. Finitely many such neighborhoods cover the fibre; their union O has compact closed complement. The complement of rho(Y\O) is a base neighborhood U with rho^{-1}(U)⊂O. Surjectivity gives F<t on U, hence F*(x)≤t. Arbitrary thresholds prove the assertion, also when the fibre maximum is −∞. No openness is used. If rho is OPEN, the image of every source neighborhood is a base neighborhood, and the same definition gives the stronger pointwise identity (F composed with rho)*=F* composed with rho.

Suppose positive finite kernels kappa_x have ENTIRE fibre support and Th(x)=integral h d kappa_x is continuous for EVERY real continuous source test h. Then rho is open. For y in open O, compact-Hausdorff normality supplies a nonnegative continuous cutoff supported in O and positive at y. Full support makes Th(rho(y))>0. Its positive locus is an open neighborhood contained in rho(O); these neighborhoods cover rho(O). No uniform positive lower bound on individual weights is needed.

For a normal local-domain target with EVERY minimal source component dominating it, sum G331's kernels on the domain quotients. Every fibre point occurs on a dominating component with positive weight, and restriction of every continuous source test is continuous there. The sum has full support and continuous integrals, so the boundary map is open. Vertical components invalidate this argument: zero generic/top-degree weight does not remove their points.

notes.summary: Reduced finite-flat determinant Artinian kernels, genuine PRIMARY coefficient maxima, and actual C/D transfer.
notes.detailedSummary: Basis/family/base-change norm trace retains every special-fibre nilpotent and inseparable length. Dense all-function tests prove full support and continuity; finite sums preserve actual decreasing D. Direct characteristic coefficients plus primary truncation prove positive maxima. Normal/no-vertical maxima are reconstructed through normal splitting and full descent.
notes.text:
Let R→B be reduced finite locally free of rank d>0. Choose a basis over local R. For finite R-module generators g_j of a B-ideal J, multiplication by h=sum T_j g_j has characteristic polynomial t^d+sum_{i=1}^d(−1)^i c_i(T)t^{d−i}. Let C_i(J) be the coefficient ideal of c_i(T) and N(J)=C_d(J). Basis changes conjugate the matrix. Generator changes substitute linear forms in T in both directions, proving coefficient-ideal independence. The determinant on the top exterior power proves arbitrary base-change compatibility and multiplicativity. This is the complete immediate Stacks 0BD2 CURRENT 31.18.6 construction at its actual finite-locally-free hypotheses; its proof was read. If J contains a^N B, redundantly include base elements x in a^N. The pure coefficient x^d belongs to N(J), so N(J) contains a boundary power and is unit-or-primary.

At ANY support P first enter the valued field K=Frac(R/P). B tensor_R K may be NONREDUCED despite reduced B. In a finite normal extension splitting its residue fields it decomposes into Artinian local factors of lengths l_j, with sum l_j=d. Multiplication on each factor is its residue scalar plus a nilpotent map, so the characteristic polynomial is product_j(t−h_j)^{l_j}. These lengths retain generic inseparability AND special-fibre nilpotence. Extend the valuation to the integral closure in the splitting field and evaluate the residue homomorphisms from B, obtaining centered lifts w_j. Then v(N(J))=sum_j l_j w_j(J). To prove this, minimum coefficient valuation of polynomials is multiplicative: quotient the support, divide each nonzero polynomial by a least-valued coefficient, and reduce to nonzero residue polynomials whose product is nonzero. Apply this Gauss argument to the determinant factorization. Boundary powers ensure finite ideal values.

The measures kappa_v=sum l_j delta_{w_j} have mass d. Their integrals on ideal gauges are determined by the coefficient identity. The ideal-difference lattice is dense in ALL real continuous source functions: it contains constants, separates via (b)+a^N B and semilocal center-separating ideals, and satisfies min(v(I)−v(J),v(K)−v(H))=v(IH+KJ)−v(JH). Compact lattice approximation from G331 gives density. Equal mass therefore gives choice independence on every continuous test, hence of the measures. Conversely any fibre point has a residue-field embedding into a splitting field; extending that particular lift makes it occur with positive Artinian length. Choice independence proves FULL fibre support and cardinality at most d. The coefficient identity first, then density and fixed mass, proves continuity on all continuous tests. Consequently n1 proves openness.

The trace tau H=integral H d kappa_v sends −w(J)/q to −v(N(J))/q and preserves C. It also preserves D by applying it to an ACTUAL decreasing C representation. Finite positive sums commute with decreasing nonpositive extended nets: at finite limits directedness approximates all finitely many summands simultaneously; a bottom summand with positive weight forces bottom. This covers partial bottom without a measurable-net integration theorem.

The direct maximum is positive. Write m=min_{rho(w)=v} w(J). Then m=min_i v(C_i(J))/i. All roots of multiplication by a generator have value at least m, so every degree-i coefficient has value at least im. For the reverse choose a generator attaining m at a fibre point. Its characteristic equation cannot have every nonleading coefficient of value strictly greater than im, since then the leading root power is uniquely least-valued. Some specialized coefficient has value at most im; that coefficient is an R-linear combination of the family coefficients. This proves the formula even with cancellation and inseparable roots.

The C_i need not be primary. Set L=sup_X v(C_d)/d, finite because C_d contains a boundary power, and choose INTEGER N>dL. Replace C_i by C_i+a^N, genuinely unit-or-primary. Their values are truncated at N. Since m≤L and N/i>L, the minimum is unchanged. Therefore rho_max(−w(J)/q)=max_i{−v(C_i+a^N)/(qi)} belongs to C_R. Fibre maximum is 1-Lipschitz for uniform norm, hence preserves C. It commutes with actual decreasing nets on finite fibres: if each limiting value is below a finite threshold, one common index puts all finitely many values below it. Thus it preserves D.

For normal-domain targets without vertical components, positive maxima follow separately from the full qualified G331 kernels. On each dominating domain quotient pass to the integral closure in a finite normal splitting field. The maximum of finitely many embedding pullbacks belongs to C or D upstairs. Full-support kernel independence identifies it with the entire fibre maximum and makes it constant on every splitting-field restriction fibre. G331's positive full-fibre descent gives membership downstairs. Maximize across finitely many dominating components; every source point is covered. This proves positive C,D maxima and actual finite-fibre decreasing passage. Both positivity and openness have been established; topology alone does not prove positivity.

notes.summary: Specified whole-section USC E, selected positive domain, open-map equality and exact general constrained-conductor rule.
notes.detailedSummary: All bounded-above extended USC obstacles including partial bottom. E positive iff actual greatest D competitor; finite continuous raw C=D, positivity iff raw continuous, then C. Normal/no-vertical and reduced flat maps have exact regularized equality/positive-domain equivalence. Arbitrary injections use full fibre maximum and require constrained regularization both D and fibre constant.
notes.text:
For bounded-above extended USC phi on the ENTIRE compact X_R, including partial −∞, define p_R phi=sup{u in D_R:u≤phi} and EXACTLY E_R phi=(p_R phi)* using ordinary whole-section USC regularization. Bottom is a competitor, and p_R phi≤E_R phi≤min(phi,0). Positivity is not part of this definition.

E_R phi belongs to D_R iff the competitor family has an ACTUAL greatest D_R member. If E is positive, the inequality makes it a competitor, so E=p. Conversely a greatest member equals p and is USC, hence equals its regularization. This includes all-bottom obstacles.

For finite continuous f, raw C and D suprema agree. If u in D lies below f, an actual decreasing C representation g_alpha→u has, for every epsilon>0, one term g_alpha<f+epsilon everywhere: strict-test continuous open sets cover the compact section, and directedness selects a common index. Then g_alpha−epsilon belongs to C, lies below f, and dominates u−epsilon. Let epsilon tend to zero. This does not assert the same reduction for arbitrary USC obstacles. The common raw p is finite and LSC, since it is a supremum of continuous competitors and a sufficiently negative constant is admissible. Thus E_R f is positive iff p_R f is continuous, and then E=p belongs to C. Indeed positivity makes p USC as well. Conversely, if p is continuous, choose competitors within epsilon at each point; neighborhoods, a finite subcover and finite maxima produce a C competitor uniformly within epsilon. Uniform closure gives p in C.

On reduced curves the granted geometric class is the full extended nonpositive branch orthant, so E phi=min(phi,0). Empty sections have their unique empty function. This is a selected positive domain, not universal positive-envelope existence. At the qualified smooth BFJ scope, G331 identifies D with the full canonical BFJ all-semivaluation class with bottom adjoined. Hence E is exactly the USC supremum of that SAME class; any smooth envelope with this signature and an actual greatest competitor agrees by the criterion. A published fixed-skeleton nef-divisor envelope has a narrower obstacle signature, from which general smooth USC-obstacle existence is not inferred.

For either map class in n2—normal-domain target with no vertical components, or reduced finite-flat—every bounded-above extended USC obstacle satisfies p_B(phi composed with rho)=p_R phi composed with rho. Pullback gives one inequality. For the other, take a source D competitor; its entire fibre maximum is a downstairs D competitor below phi and dominates the source function on every lift. The map is open by n1–n2, so the pointwise regularization identity gives E_B(phi composed with rho)=E_R phi composed with rho. This equality of FUNCTIONS holds even outside the positive domain. Full positive descent gives exact equivalence of the two positive domains. For finite continuous obstacles their positive outputs are C. Both positive maxima and openness are used; raw extrema alone are insufficient.

For ANY reduced finite injection define E_{B,fib} by taking only FULL-fibre-constant D_B competitors below phi composed with rho, followed by ordinary upstairs USC regularization. G331 identifies its raw supremum with p_R phi composed with rho. The compact quotient lemma gives EXACTLY E_R phi(x)=max_{rho(y)=x} E_{B,fib}(phi composed with rho)(y). Downstairs positivity holds iff this constrained upstairs regularization is BOTH in D_B AND constant on EVERY fibre. For the forward direction, positive downstairs E equals p; its USC pullback is already the constrained regularization. Conversely a positive fibre-constant constrained regularization descends positively, lies below phi and above p_R phi, and hence equals p_R phi and E_R phi. Regularization does not automatically retain fibre constancy.

The unconstrained source E dominates the constrained E. The universal comparison is therefore rho*E_R phi≤M_fib(E_B(phi composed with rho)), where M_fib repeats the maximum over the full fibre. Without openness it does NOT imply rho*E_R phi≤E_B pointwise. If E_B is positive, equality E_B=rho*E_R holds exactly when E_B is FULL-fibre constant: its positive descent is then the greatest downstairs competitor. If both envelopes are positive, pulled downstairs E is a source competitor and gives the pointwise inequality, with equality still requiring full constancy. For normalization every conductor quotient fibre, nonminimal support and lower-dimensional point is included.

notes.summary: Entire all-field node: source actual C(−1,−2), downstairs E nonD, reversed ONE lift inequality.

Whole-section regularization raises shared point to −1 and violates second-plane regular order domination. notes.text:
Over ANY field k take R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy), S=A_1×A_2 with A_1=k[x,z]_(x,z), A_2=k[y,z]_(y,z), and T=k[z]_(z). Restriction at x=0 and y=0 gives R=A_1×_T A_2. Local denominators lift with the same nonzero constant term, proving the localized fibre product. S is finite, generated by its two idempotents, and is the normalization. The conductor c=(x,y): a conductor element must have zero common residue in T, and that condition suffices. Thus R/c=T and S/c=T×T. There is exactly one nontrivial FULL boundary fibre: w_1 killing x on A_1 and w_2 killing y on A_2, both inducing ord_z on T. Its base point is v_0. All other fibres are singletons. Normalize by m=(x,y,z).

The finite continuous obstacle is f(v)=−1−1/v(y), with 1/∞=0. On A_1 it is −1; on A_2 it lies in [−2,−1]. Let o_i be ordinary regular order on plane i. For every primary J and normalized w, J⊂m_i^{o_i(J)} implies w(J)≥o_i(J). Thus u(w)≤u(o_i) for all C functions and then all actual D limits, including bottom. Since f(o_2)=−2, the actual greatest source competitor is p_S=E_S=(−1,−2). It belongs to C_S, represented by the semilocal primary ideal m_1×m_2², and lies below f. These upper bounds prove greatestness for D, not merely ideal profiles.

For every integer N≥2 set alpha=1/(N−1) and h_{1,N}(w)=−(1−alpha)−alpha min(w(x),Nw(z)). It is a C profile using the genuine proper PRIMARY ideal (x,z^N). Since min(w(x),w(z))=1, its minimum is at least one, so h_{1,N}≤−1. At w_1 it equals −2. Pair it with constant −2 on A_2. This tuple agrees on the ENTIRE shared fibre and descends positively through G331 to a C_R competitor. Every first-plane point other than w_1 has finite w(x): killing x leaves the one-dimensional regular T with its singleton normalized section. At each such point h_{1,N} tends to −1. On the whole second plane every downstairs competitor is at most −2 by the regular-order bound. Consequently the raw C and D suprema are −1 on the first plane off v_0, and −2 on the WHOLE second plane including v_0.

Monomial valuations w_M(x)=M,w_M(z)=1 converge on EVERY polynomial and local denominator to w_1: transverse terms acquire unbounded value, surviving z terms retain their orders, and denominators have value zero. This is valid in every characteristic. Thus whole-section regularization raises v_0 to −1. At a second-plane point other than v_0, the compact first-plane image is closed and absent, so a neighborhood avoids it. Therefore E_R f is −1 on the ENTIRE first plane including v_0 and −2 on the second plane off v_0. Its pullback is USC on both planes, hence it is USC by the compact quotient. But it is NOT D_R: on the second plane its value −1 at w_2 exceeds its value −2 at o_2, contradicting the proved domination inequality.

At the second lift, rho*E_R f(w_2)=−1>−2=E_S(f composed with rho)(w_2), a genuine reversed gap ONE for the SPECIFIED regularized operator. The constrained upstairs raw supremum is the pullback of the computed downstairs raw function. Its ordinary regularization is (−1,−2): w_1 is raised on the first plane, while the second remains constantly −2. Hence E_{S,fib} is positive continuous but NOT fibre constant. Its full fibre maximum is exactly E_R f, checking n3's quotient formula at every point and the necessity of BOTH conditions.

The degree-one generic branch traces of (−1,−2) have incompatible limits at the shared conductor point, so no unrestricted continuous degree trace can be invented. Also S tensor_R S=A_1×T×T×A_2; the two vertical T components are real support/fibre data and cannot be dropped.

notes.summary: Closed-image and normal-target vertical counterexamples have positive continuous envelopes at both ends.

Vertical injection R→R times R/(xy) has nonopen isolated source point and the same positive gap. Intrinsic curve and ambient surface product arities remain distinct.
notes.text:
For a noninjective finite map factor through its literal reduced image A=R/ker. Ideal restriction, uniform limits and actual decreasing representations give C_R→C_A and D_R→D_A, without surjectivity. If E_R phi is positive, its restriction is an intrinsic competitor, so (E_R phi)|_{X_A}≤E_A(phi|_{X_A}). Positivity is needed: arbitrary nonpositive regularizations are not competitors. No ambient extension or restriction equality follows from a closed boundary embedding.

An all-field example has positive CONTINUOUS outputs at both ends. Let R=k[x,y]_(x,y), Q=R/(xy), gauge m, and f=−1/v(x), continuous in [−1,0]. The curve points are w_x(x)=1,w_x(y)=∞ and w_y(x)=∞,w_y(y)=1. On the regular surface ordinary order o satisfies u(v)≤u(o) for all C,D functions by the primary-ideal order argument in n4. Since f(o)=−1, every competitor is at most −1 everywhere. Constant −1 is admissible; thus p_R f=E_R f=−1 in C_R.

On Q the proper primary profiles −v((x^N,y))/N equal (−1,−1/N) and converge uniformly to (−1,0). The restricted obstacle itself belongs to C_Q, so E_Q(f|_{X_Q})=(−1,0). The restriction inequality has exact gap ONE at w_y. No D_R extension of that tuple exists: G331's normal zero dichotomy says a D function zero at any point on a normal local branch is identically zero, contradicting the value −1 at w_x. This is an actual geometric extension obstruction. The ambient lifts of these profiles increase to zero where v(y)<∞ and −1 where v(y)=∞; the limit is not USC because monomial (1,M) tends to w_x. No increasing closure is available.

Intrinsic and ambient products have different arities: G345 gives mu_R(−1)=delta_o on the surface and mu_Q()=delta_{w_x}+delta_{w_y} on the curve. Q has zero ambient degree-two contribution as an R-module, without erasing its intrinsic reference measure or points.

Now inject the NORMAL target R into reduced finite B=R×Q by r↦(r,bar r). The source E for the pulled obstacle is the actual C_B tuple (−1,(−1,0)); base E is −1. Both are positive continuous, with gap ONE at the vertical lift w_y. That source point is isolated on its clopen finite curve section, but its image is not open in X_R, since monomial valuations (M,1) approach it. Thus the boundary map is nonopen. The entire fibre maximum is zero at that base point and −1 elsewhere; it is neither continuous nor D_R, by normal zero dichotomy. The dominating norm trace ignores vertical generic weight and consequently lacks full fibre support. Normality ALONE cannot replace the no-vertical hypothesis. All supports and lower-dimensional points remain.

notes.text:
Let n=dim R≥1 and p=n−1. For finite reduced B and each closed center q over m write f_q=[kappa(q):kappa(m)]. Define the AMBIENT product mu_B^[R](H_1,…,H_p)=sum_{dim B_q=n} f_q mu_{B_q}(H_1|_q,…,H_p|_q). Lower-dimensional centers have zero ambient degree-n contribution, while their points and intrinsic lower-arity products remain. For each top minimal P of R set K_P=Frac(R/P), d_P=dim_{K_P}(B tensor_R K_P), and let j_P:X_{R/P}→X_R be the literal supported inclusion. Missing generic components have d_P=0. For every bounded actual D_R tuple,

rho_* mu_B^[R](rho*u_1,…,rho*u_p)=sum_{dim R/P=n} d_P j_{P,*} mu_{R/P}(j_P*u_1,…,j_P*u_p).

For noninjective maps rho means restriction to the exact image followed by inclusion. All supports are retained. A scalar degree occurs only if all top d_P=d, when the right side is d mu_R(tuple).

FIRST reconstruct geometric projection. Use n1's actual finite PRIMARY source models and common product-primary refinements for core inputs and tests. Pulled exceptional equations remain regular on surviving reduced components. On Spec R use delta(P)=dim R/P; excellence gives universal catenarity and the finite-type transcendence-degree extension in complete Stacks 02QL Situation 42.7.1. Each top model component has delta-dimension n. For a proper dominant source integral top component over an integral base component, of full function-field degree delta_Q, complete Stacks 0AYA 42.26.3 gives the ACTUAL cycle equality f_*[f*E]_{n−1}=delta_Q[E]_{n−1}. It is used BEFORE Chow quotients and includes inseparability. Its norm/divisor foundation 42.18.1 is disclosed recursive published background, not a freshly reread proof.

At a top exceptional generic point the reduced local ring is one-dimensional. Embed it into the sum of component domains; the cokernel has finite length. Multiplication by a regular Cartier equation has equal kernel and cokernel lengths on that cokernel, so the Cartier-divisor length is the sum of the component lengths. Generic reduced component weights are one, but ALL Cartier thickness remains. Closed-fibre cycles are proper over residue FIELDS, so complete Stacks 0BEL 33.45.7 gives numerical projection with residue-field dimensions. For a supported Cartier scheme only over an Artinian R-quotient, including mixed characteristic, filter by m-powers first: coherent layers are proper over kappa(m), Euler characteristics add, and their generic thickness lengths add. This is G345's supported Euler/Koszul construction, not misuse of a FIELD lemma on a mixed-characteristic thickening. Cycle and numerical projection establish the displayed pairing formula with all f_q.

Core evaluations are n1's quotient-support lattices. G345 compares its independent geometric measure with these supported pairings by an ACTUAL fixed-primary section-image identity on ONE common model. Uniform convergence of arbitrary Cartier functions is not assumed to imply intersection convergence. Neither arbitrary-model cofinality nor finite Cartier determination of a trace is needed.

Here is the full algebraic verification. For primary labels I_1,…,I_r and P_s=product I_i^{s_i}, complete CURRENT Swanson–Huneke 17.4.1–3 supplies eventual module quotient-length polynomials and degree-n form H_M(s)=sum_{|a|=n} e_R(I_1^[a_1],…,I_r^[a_r];M)s^a/(a_1!…a_r!), zero for dim M<n. The complete setup and immediate proof were read at arbitrary Noetherian local hypotheses. No coefficient inequality is inferred from polynomial domination.

For 0→M_1→M_2→M_3→0, the multigraded intersection module direct-sum_s(P_sM_2 intersect M_1) is a submodule of the finite multi-Rees module of M_2. Finite homogeneous generation, the complete 17.1.6 Artin–Rees argument, gives common vector c with P_sM_1⊂P_sM_2 intersect M_1⊂P_{s−c}M_1 for large coordinatewise s. The outside length polynomials have the same top form because a constant shift changes only lower order. On every positive rational ray their difference is lower order; squeezing gives that same homogeneous form for the middle quotient. Polynomial identity then identifies forms globally. The ACTUAL quotient exact sequence gives H_{M_2}=H_{M_1}+H_{M_3}. This reconstructs 17.4.4 without assuming reduction modulo P_s is left exact.

A finite module has a finite prime filtration: choose an element with maximal annihilator, which is prime since if ab kills it and b does not, the annihilator of b times it would be strictly larger unless a was already in the annihilator. Repeat on quotients; Noetherianity terminates the ascending submodule chain. Apply top-form additivity. For top minimal P, reduced R_P is a field, so the number of filtration factors surviving there is dim_{K_P}(B tensor_R K_P)=d_P. Other factors have smaller dimension. Thus H_B=sum d_P H_{R/P}, and H_R=sum H_{R/P}. The generic reduced finite algebra is a product of fields, so d_P sums FULL field degrees, including inseparability.

For every primary product the finite Artinian quotient decomposes into closed-center factors, and composition series give EXACTLY length_R(B/P_sB)=sum_q f_q length_{B_q}(B_q/P_sB_q). No separable-degree replacement is permitted. Comparing top forms proves every mixed ideal moment, agreeing with the preceding geometric projection. G345's rational-profile moments, input denominators and every ideal-gauge test establish the displayed measure formula on rational tuples. Dense ideal differences on the ENTIRE section and reference mass identify Radon measures. Uniform rational approximation gives C via weak uniform continuity. For bounded D use ACTUAL decreasing C representations with a common bound; quotient and pullback preserve their prescribed D limits by G331. G345's NET theorem applies to each factor. Fixed continuous tests, compact pushforward and finite sums pass to the limit; no measurable-net monotone convergence is used.

Normalization has top d_P=1 and yields the full closed-residue-weighted conductor pushforward. Compatible upstairs bounded tuples descend positively; push along the FULL quotient adds any masses on identified fibres. Curves have zero inputs and reference measure sum_q f_q ord_q(a) delta_{ord_q/ord_q(a)}; DVR freeness and parameter length give the curve finite-map formula. Dimension zero is empty with zero measure. For an originally nonreduced algebra this theorem uses its reduction and REDUCED generic degrees, not its original nilpotent rank. SH17.4.7's literal unquotiented colon term is not used: the finite correction is the annihilator in the CURRENT quotient by previous parameters, derived from17.4.6 and confirmed on the source page.

notes.text:
